question.text: A fund manager explains to the Investment Committee: 'Enterprise Value reflects the operating value of the business regardless of capital structure, while Equity Value reflects the value of the shareholders' residual claim'. Which ONE of the following correctly expresses the EV-to-Equity-Value bridge?

answer.text: Equity Value = EV - EBITDA + Working Capital
Equity Value = EV x (1 - Debt/Equity ratio)
Equity Value = EV + Total Debt + Preference Capital - Cash
Equity Value = EV - Total Debt (net of cash) - Preference Capital

explanation.text: The Logic: EV = Equity Value + Total Debt (net of cash) + Preference Capital. Rearranged, Equity Value = EV - Total Debt (net of cash) - Preference Capital. EV measures the debt-free, cash-free value of the operating business; the residual after subtracting senior claims belongs to equity holders. The Trap: Option B is a ratio manipulation that has no grounding in the EV bridge. Option C reverses the sign of the bridge and would inflate equity value by the very claims that should be subtracted. Option A mixes an operating metric (EBITDA) and a balance-sheet item (working capital) in a way that does not correspond to the bridge. Note: 'Net of cash' means cash and cash equivalents are deducted from gross debt before the subtraction — surplus cash effectively belongs to equity holders.
